sourcing_note: Targeted sourcing derived from a backward simulation of select_frozen_cohort(seed=100100) against the current pool: the selected 120-event cohort was short 4 of the required >=40 negative events even though the pool-wide aggregate already exceeds 40, because the fixed seed's stratum/year shuffle doesn't distribute negative events proportionally. A greedy search (add one hypothetical negative candidate at a time to whichever (stratum, year) slot most increases the selected-cohort negative count, re-simulating after each addition) found that REGULATORY/2018, REGULATORY/2019 and REGULATORY/2024 are the most efficient real slots to fill - REGULATORY needs only 3 more negative events pool-wide to close the full 4-event gap in the selected cohort (versus 5 for PHASE_3_PIVOTAL or 9 for PHASE_2_POC). All three candidates below are FDA Complete Response Letters sourced from the openFDA CRL transparency dataset (api.fda.gov/transparency/crl.json) and cross-verified against the issuer's own SEC 8-K disclosure.

events.notes: FDA CRL for IV meloxicam (first of two - a second CRL followed in March 2019, not sourced here). Release states the pivotal Phase 3 trials were statistically significant on primary endpoints but the CRL cited ad hoc/secondary-endpoint analgesic-effect concerns and CMC extractable/leachable questions; contemporaneous coverage ('Recro plummets on CRL') confirms an unambiguous negative market reaction, not a mixed disclosure.

FDA CRL for golodirsen (accelerated approval NDA) cited infection risk from IV infusion ports and pre-clinical renal toxicity concerns; issuer's own release quotes leadership as 'very surprised' - unambiguous negative surprise. This is a distinct, earlier, separate catalyst from REG-2023-SRPT-ELEVIDYS (already in the pool, a 2023 approval for a different asset); Sarepta now has 2 pool events, well under the 5-event issuer cap.

FDA CRL for KRESLADI (lentiviral gene therapy) requesting additional CMC (manufacturing) information; clinical safety and efficacy data were not cited as deficiencies, making this a comparatively milder CRL type (CMC-only, similar in kind to a rejected 2018 Evolus/DWP-450 CRL candidate that failed the liquidity floor and was not used), but it is still a genuine regulatory rejection and delay to approval - the issuer's own release and contemporaneous coverage ('Rocket gene therapy rejected by FDA over manufacturing') confirm this, unlike Evolus's own release, which bundled its CRL together with a separate positive manufacturing-facility inspection result in one 'progress' headline.
